t0.narrative: Markets enter H2 2026 with macro uncertainty dominated by the Fed's rate path and fiscal policy outlook. Sector rotation signals a shift from mega-cap tech toward cyclicals and value as rate-cut expectations firm. Key risk events include upcoming CPI/PCE prints, Q2 earnings season kickoff, and geopolitical tensions in the South China Sea and Ukraine. Without live data feeds, confidence is severely constrained — this briefing should be treated as a structural template pending connector enrichment.

sections.title: 宏观信号 (Macro Regime)
sections.summary: Fed policy trajectory, inflation dynamics, and growth indicators form the macro backdrop. The rate-cutting cycle that began in September 2024 is the dominant regime-defining feature.
bullets: Fed: Rate-cutting cycle underway since Sep 2024 (50bp inaugural cut). Market pricing for additional cuts in H2 2026 — exact trajectory dependent on inflation and labor data.
Inflation: Core PCE trended toward 2.5-3.0% through late 2024 / early 2025. Progress toward 2% target is uneven — shelter and services remain sticky.
Growth: GDP growth resilient through 2024-25 at 2.5-3.0% annualized. No recession signal from leading indicators as of late 2024, but fiscal impulse fading.
Labor: Payroll gains cooling toward 150-175K/month. Unemployment ~4.0-4.2%. Wage growth moderating — positive for inflation outlook.
Dollar (DXY): Direction hinges on rate differential path. USD weakened post-Sep-2024 cut; trend depends on ECB/BOJ divergence.
Yield Curve: 10Y-2Y inversion persisted through 2024. If un-inversion occurred in 2025-26, recession clock starts but with long and variable lags.

sections.title: 板块轮动 (Sector Rotation)
sections.summary: As the rate cycle turns, capital is rotating from rate-sensitive growth names toward cyclicals, value, and rate-beneficiary sectors.
bullets: Tech (XLK): Mega-cap AI-driven rally dominated 2024-25. Valuation concerns and rotation pressure may cap upside in H2 2026. Watch semiconductor sub-sector as lead indicator.
Financials (XLF): Primary beneficiary of rate normalization. Steepening yield curve supports NIM expansion. Regional bank consolidation and deregulation tailwinds.
Energy (XLE): Oil price range $70-85 WTI through 2024. Geopolitical supply risk (Middle East, Russia sanctions) balanced against demand slowdown fears.
Industrials (XLI): Infrastructure spending (IRA, CHIPS Act) provides multi-year tailwind. Re-shoring trend supports domestic manufacturing.
Healthcare (XLV): Defensive with GLP-1 innovation cycle. Biotech funding recovery dependent on rate path.
Consumer Discretionary (XLY): Bifurcated — luxury/high-end resilient; lower-income cohort under pressure from cumulative inflation.
Real Estate (XLRE): Rate-sensitive; benefits directly from cut cycle. Commercial real estate stress (office) vs data center boom (AI demand).
Utilities (XLU): AI data center power demand is a structural growth story. Grid investment cycle supports multi-year capex.

sections.title: 风险事件 (Risk Events)
sections.summary: Multiple risk vectors — geopolitical, economic-data-surprise, earnings, and liquidity — require active monitoring.
bullets: Geopolitical — South China Sea: Taiwan Strait tensions elevated. Any escalation disrupts semiconductor supply chain (TSMC) and broader technology sector.
Geopolitical — Ukraine/Russia: Conflict in sustained stalemate. Energy and grain price spillover remains a tail risk. Western sanctions regime steady.
Geopolitical — Middle East: Red Sea / Hormuz transit risk. Oil supply disruption remains the primary transmission mechanism.
Data Risk: CPI/PCE prints with >0.2% deviation from consensus can swing rate expectations by 25-50bp. Employment data (NFP) is the other binary event.
Earnings Risk: Q2 2026 season begins mid-July. Guidance dispersion is elevated — AI capex ROI is the key thematic question for tech.
Liquidity Risk: Treasury General Account (TGA) drawdown and QT taper affect reserves. Money market fund AUM at record — rate cuts may trigger rotation into duration.
Event Risk — US Election 2026: Midterm election in November. Fiscal policy uncertainty rises into Q3/Q4. Potential for government shutdown drama in Sep-Oct FY budget cycle.

evidence.claim: Fed began cutting rates in September 2024 with a 50bp move
evidence.support: FOMC Sep 2024 statement and Summary of Economic Projections

evidence.claim: Inflation moderated but remains above 2% target as of early 2025
evidence.support: CPI YoY trended from 3.7% (Sep 2023) to ~2.7% (late 2024). Core PCE ~2.6-2.8%.

evidence.claim: Sector rotation from growth to value/cyclicals typically accompanies rate-cut cycles
evidence.support: Historical factor performance: value and size factors outperform growth in the 12 months following first cut (Fama-French data 1970-2020)

evidence.claim: AI infrastructure spend is a structural growth driver for utilities and industrials
evidence.support: Hyperscaler capex (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META) exceeded $150B combined in 2024 with guidance for further increases

evidence.claim: Commercial real estate stress concentrated in office sector; data center is bright spot
evidence.support: Office vacancy rates at multi-decade highs in major US metros. Data center vacancy near zero with pre-leasing strong.

evidence.claim: Geopolitical risk premia elevated across Taiwan Strait, Ukraine, and Middle East
evidence.support: DoD posture statements, satellite imagery of force dispositions, insurance premia for Red Sea transit

evidence.claim: 2026 US midterm election introduces fiscal policy uncertainty in H2
evidence.support: Structural pattern: midterm years see elevated policy uncertainty index (Baker-Bloom-Davis EPU) in Q3-Q4
